drugs.acute_risks: Fluoxetine Hydrochloride. Early agitation, and with the wrong mix, serotonin syndrome or a blood-pressure crisis. Overdose of older tricyclics can stop the heart. An antidepressant name on a public medicine listing. Serotonin syndrome and bleeding are the mix risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Fluoxetine Hydrochloride. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Fluoxetine Hydrochloride. Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Fluoxetine Hydrochloride. They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Fluoxetine Hydrochloride. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Fluoxetine Hydrochloride. Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Fluoxetine Hydrochloride. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Fluoxetine Hydrochloride. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.
drugs.testing: Fluoxetine Hydrochloride. Not a reagent-test problem. The risk is the name on the packet plus whatever else is taken.
drugs.harm_reduction: Fluoxetine Hydrochloride. Do not combine an MAOI with an SSRI, a stimulant, tramadol, or DXM. Do not stop suddenly without the prescriber. This file has no dose.

heart rhythm disturbance
nausea
drugs.acute_risks: Allantoin, Benzethonium Chloride, Lidocaine HCl. Loss of the airway, stopped breathing, and for local anaesthetics, seizures and cardiac arrest if they reach the blood in quantity. drugs.chronic_risks: Allantoin, Benzethonium Chloride, Lidocaine HCl. Repeated nonmedical use of volatile anaesthetics injures organs and can sensitise the heart.
drugs.overdose_signs: Allantoin, Benzethonium Chloride, Lidocaine HCl. Unresponsiveness and no reliable breathing. This is an emergency. Do not wait.
drugs.dependence: Allantoin, Benzethonium Chloride, Lidocaine HCl. Not the usual pattern, except where the drug is also a sedative people return to.
drugs.tolerance: Allantoin, Benzethonium Chloride, Lidocaine HCl. Not a useful idea outside anaesthesia. The step from sedated to not breathing is small.
drugs.withdrawal: Allantoin, Benzethonium Chloride, Lidocaine HCl. Not the main harm.
drugs.medical_uses: Allantoin, Benzethonium Chloride, Lidocaine HCl. Surgery, procedures, and local pain control, with monitoring.
drugs.contraindications: Allantoin, Benzethonium Chloride, Lidocaine HCl. No airway support, other sedatives, and certain heart conditions for local anaesthetics.
drugs.testing: Allantoin, Benzethonium Chloride, Lidocaine HCl. There is no home test that makes an anaesthetic safe to use.
drugs.harm_reduction: Allantoin, Benzethonium Chloride, Lidocaine HCl. These drugs belong where someone can breathe for the person. This file has no dose and no method.

drugs.acute_risks: Morphine Sulfate. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Morphine Sulfate. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Morphine Sulfate. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Morphine Sulfate. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Morphine Sulfate. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Morphine Sulfate. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Morphine Sulfate. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Morphine Sulfate. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Morphine Sulfate. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Morphine Sulfate. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Phentermine Hydrochloride. Heart attack, stroke, seizure, overheating, and agitated psychosis. Risk rises with other stimulants, dehydration, and confined hot spaces. A stimulant name on a public medicine listing. Heart strain, overheating, and a second stimulant are the acute risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Phentermine Hydrochloride. Dependence, exhaustion, weight loss, heart injury, tooth and nasal damage for some, and persistent anxiety or psychosis.
drugs.overdose_signs: Phentermine Hydrochloride. Chest pain, collapsing, extreme agitation, very high temperature, seizures, or a pounding heart. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Phentermine Hydrochloride. Psychological dependence is common. Some stimulants also cause a severe crash.
drugs.tolerance: Phentermine Hydrochloride. The wanted effect fades faster than the strain on the heart.
drugs.withdrawal: Phentermine Hydrochloride. Exhaustion, hunger, low mood, and strong cravings. Suicidal thoughts can appear in the crash.
drugs.medical_uses: Phentermine Hydrochloride. A few are licensed for attention or sleep disorders. Most stimulant material outside a pharmacy is unregulated.
drugs.contraindications: Phentermine Hydrochloride. Heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, psychosis, pregnancy, and MAOI medicines.
drugs.testing: Phentermine Hydrochloride. Reagents can suggest a class and still miss dangerous substitutes such as PMA, synthetic cathinones, or fentanyl in a pressed pill.
drugs.harm_reduction: Phentermine Hydrochloride. Overheating and chest pain are emergencies. Do not mix with other stimulants or MAOIs. This file has no dose and no source.

drugs.acute_risks: Bupropion Hcl Er (xl). Early agitation, and with the wrong mix, serotonin syndrome or a blood-pressure crisis. Overdose of older tricyclics can stop the heart. An antidepressant name on a public medicine listing. Serotonin syndrome and bleeding are the mix risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Bupropion Hcl Er (xl). Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Bupropion Hcl Er (xl). Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Bupropion Hcl Er (xl). They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Bupropion Hcl Er (xl). Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Bupropion Hcl Er (xl). Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Bupropion Hcl Er (xl). Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Bupropion Hcl Er (xl). MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.

drugs.chronic_risks: Buprenorphine Sublingual. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Buprenorphine Sublingual. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Buprenorphine Sublingual. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Buprenorphine Sublingual. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Buprenorphine Sublingual. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Buprenorphine Sublingual. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Buprenorphine Sublingual. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Buprenorphine Sublingual. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Buprenorphine Sublingual. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Oxymorphone Hydrochloride. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Oxymorphone Hydrochloride. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Oxymorphone Hydrochloride. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Oxymorphone Hydrochloride. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Oxymorphone Hydrochloride. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Oxymorphone Hydrochloride. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Oxymorphone Hydrochloride. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Oxymorphone Hydrochloride. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Oxymorphone Hydrochloride. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Oxymorphone Hydrochloride. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Midazolam Hydrochloride. Amnesia, injury, and sexual vulnerability during blackouts. With alcohol or opioids, breathing can stop. drugs.chronic_risks: Midazolam Hydrochloride. Dependence, worsened anxiety between uses, falls in older people, and a hard withdrawal.

drugs.harm_reduction: Midazolam Hydrochloride. Do not mix with opioids or alcohol. Do not stop regular use suddenly. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Tramadol Hydrochloride. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Tramadol Hydrochloride. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Tramadol Hydrochloride. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Tramadol Hydrochloride. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Tramadol Hydrochloride. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Tramadol Hydrochloride. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Tramadol Hydrochloride. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Tramadol Hydrochloride. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Tramadol Hydrochloride. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Tramadol Hydrochloride. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.chronic_risks: Venlafaxine Hydrochloride. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.

drugs.acute_risks: Dexamethasone Sodium Phosphate, Bupivacaine Hydrochloride, Povidine Iodine. drugs.chronic_risks: Dexamethasone Sodium Phosphate, Bupivacaine Hydrochloride, Povidine Iodine. Repeated nonmedical use of volatile anaesthetics injures organs and can sensitise the heart.
drugs.overdose_signs: Dexamethasone Sodium Phosphate, Bupivacaine Hydrochloride, Povidine Iodine. Unresponsiveness and no reliable breathing. This is an emergency. Do not wait.
drugs.dependence: Dexamethasone Sodium Phosphate, Bupivacaine Hydrochloride, Povidine Iodine. Not the usual pattern, except where the drug is also a sedative people return to.
drugs.tolerance: Dexamethasone Sodium Phosphate, Bupivacaine Hydrochloride, Povidine Iodine. Not a useful idea outside anaesthesia. The step from sedated to not breathing is small.
drugs.withdrawal: Dexamethasone Sodium Phosphate, Bupivacaine Hydrochloride, Povidine Iodine. Not the main harm.

drugs.contraindications: Dexamethasone Sodium Phosphate, Bupivacaine Hydrochloride, Povidine Iodine. No airway support, other sedatives, and certain heart conditions for local anaesthetics.

drugs.chronic_risks: Duloxetine Hcl. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Duloxetine Hcl. Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Duloxetine Hcl. They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Duloxetine Hcl. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Duloxetine Hcl. Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Duloxetine Hcl. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Duloxetine Hcl. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.
drugs.testing: Duloxetine Hcl. Not a reagent-test problem. The risk is the name on the packet plus whatever else is taken.

drugs.chronic_risks: Tramadol Hcl. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.

drugs.harm_reduction: Methadone Hydrochloride. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Lidocaine Hydrochloride and Epinephrine Hydrochloride. Loss of the airway, stopped breathing, and for local anaesthetics, seizures and cardiac arrest if they reach the blood in quantity. An anaesthetic name on a public medicine listing. drugs.chronic_risks: Lidocaine Hydrochloride and Epinephrine Hydrochloride. Repeated nonmedical use of volatile anaesthetics injures organs and can sensitise the heart.

drugs.dependence: Lidocaine Hydrochloride and Epinephrine Hydrochloride. Not the usual pattern, except where the drug is also a sedative people return to.
drugs.tolerance: Lidocaine Hydrochloride and Epinephrine Hydrochloride. Not a useful idea outside anaesthesia. The step from sedated to not breathing is small.
drugs.withdrawal: Lidocaine Hydrochloride and Epinephrine Hydrochloride. Not the main harm.

drugs.chronic_risks: 5% Lidocaine. Repeated nonmedical use of volatile anaesthetics injures organs and can sensitise the heart.

drugs.dependence: 5% Lidocaine. Not the usual pattern, except where the drug is also a sedative people return to.
drugs.tolerance: 5% Lidocaine. Not a useful idea outside anaesthesia. The step from sedated to not breathing is small.
drugs.withdrawal: 5% Lidocaine. Not the main harm.
drugs.medical_uses: 5% Lidocaine. Surgery, procedures, and local pain control, with monitoring.

drugs.testing: 5% Lidocaine. There is no home test that makes an anaesthetic safe to use.

drugs.acute_risks: Paroxetine Hydrochloride. Early agitation, and with the wrong mix, serotonin syndrome or a blood-pressure crisis. Overdose of older tricyclics can stop the heart. An antidepressant name on a public medicine listing. Serotonin syndrome and bleeding are the mix risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Paroxetine Hydrochloride. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Paroxetine Hydrochloride. Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Paroxetine Hydrochloride. They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Paroxetine Hydrochloride. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Paroxetine Hydrochloride. Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Paroxetine Hydrochloride. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Paroxetine Hydrochloride. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.
drugs.testing: Paroxetine Hydrochloride. Not a reagent-test problem. The risk is the name on the packet plus whatever else is taken.
drugs.harm_reduction: Paroxetine Hydrochloride. Do not combine an MAOI with an SSRI, a stimulant, tramadol, or DXM. Do not stop suddenly without the prescriber. This file has no dose.

drugs.chronic_risks: Lidocaine Cream. Repeated nonmedical use of volatile anaesthetics injures organs and can sensitise the heart.

drugs.dependence: Lidocaine Cream. Not the usual pattern, except where the drug is also a sedative people return to.

drugs.withdrawal: Lidocaine Cream. Not the main harm.
drugs.medical_uses: Lidocaine Cream. Surgery, procedures, and local pain control, with monitoring.
drugs.contraindications: Lidocaine Cream. No airway support, other sedatives, and certain heart conditions for local anaesthetics.
drugs.testing: Lidocaine Cream. There is no home test that makes an anaesthetic safe to use.
drugs.harm_reduction: Lidocaine Cream. These drugs belong where someone can breathe for the person. This file has no dose and no method.

drugs.chronic_risks: Lurasidone Hydrochloride. Movement disorders, weight gain, diabetes, raised prolactin, and sedation.

drugs.withdrawal: Lurasidone Hydrochloride. Nausea, sweating, restlessness, and return of the illness being treated. This is a prescriber decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Lurasidone Hydrochloride. Psychosis, bipolar disorder, severe agitation, and a few other licensed uses.
drugs.contraindications: Lurasidone Hydrochloride. Other QT-prolonging drugs, other heavy sedatives, and for clozapine a list of blood and cardiac warnings that belong to the prescriber.

drugs.harm_reduction: Lurasidone Hydrochloride. Fever plus rigidity on one of these medicines is an emergency. Do not stack with other sedatives for sleep. This file has no dose.

effects: alertness
energy
talkativeness
reduced appetite
raised heart rate
adverse_effects: anxiety

overheating

drugs.acute_risks: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Oral. Heart attack, stroke, seizure, overheating, and agitated psychosis. Risk rises with other stimulants, dehydration, and confined hot spaces. A stimulant name on a public medicine listing. Heart strain, overheating, and a second stimulant are the acute risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Oral. Dependence, exhaustion, weight loss, heart injury, tooth and nasal damage for some, and persistent anxiety or psychosis.
drugs.overdose_signs: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Oral. Chest pain, collapsing, extreme agitation, very high temperature, seizures, or a pounding heart. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Oral. Psychological dependence is common. Some stimulants also cause a severe crash.
drugs.tolerance: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Oral. The wanted effect fades faster than the strain on the heart.
drugs.withdrawal: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Oral. Exhaustion, hunger, low mood, and strong cravings. Suicidal thoughts can appear in the crash.
drugs.medical_uses: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Oral. A few are licensed for attention or sleep disorders. Most stimulant material outside a pharmacy is unregulated.
drugs.contraindications: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Oral. Heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, psychosis, pregnancy, and MAOI medicines.
drugs.testing: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Oral. Reagents can suggest a class and still miss dangerous substitutes such as PMA, synthetic cathinones, or fentanyl in a pressed pill.
drugs.harm_reduction: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Oral. Overheating and chest pain are emergencies. Do not mix with other stimulants or MAOIs. This file has no dose and no source.

adverse_effects: vomiting

drugs.acute_risks: Pentobarbital Sodium. Unconsciousness, choking on vomit, stopped breathing, and accidents. Another sedative, opioid, or benzodiazepine makes this much more dangerous. A sedative name on a public medicine listing. With alcohol, an opioid, or another sedative it can stop breathing. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Pentobarbital Sodium. Dependence, memory injury, mood change, and for alcohol, liver, heart, and cancer risk.
drugs.overdose_signs: Pentobarbital Sodium. Cannot be woken, slow or stopped breathing, blue lips, vomiting while semi-conscious. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Pentobarbital Sodium. Physical dependence occurs with repeated heavy use of alcohol, barbiturates, GHB, and related sedatives.
drugs.tolerance: Pentobarbital Sodium. Tolerance to the feeling rises faster than tolerance to stopped breathing.
drugs.withdrawal: Pentobarbital Sodium. Alcohol, barbiturate, and GHB withdrawal can cause seizures and delirium and can be fatal. Stopping suddenly after heavy use needs medical care.
drugs.medical_uses: Pentobarbital Sodium. Some are anaesthetics, antiseizure medicines, or alcohol treatments. Others have no safe nonmedical use.
drugs.contraindications: Pentobarbital Sodium. Other sedatives, lung disease, a history of withdrawal seizures, and pregnancy.
drugs.testing: Pentobarbital Sodium. Strength of non-pharmaceutical GHB-type liquids is unknowable by looking. Reagents do not make a sedative safe.
drugs.harm_reduction: Pentobarbital Sodium. Sedative withdrawal can kill. Do not stop heavy use suddenly without medical help. Do not mix sedatives. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Aripiprazole Oral. Severe stiffness, high fever and confusion can be neuroleptic malignant syndrome, which is an emergency. Some of these drugs prolong the QT interval. drugs.chronic_risks: Aripiprazole Oral. Movement disorders, weight gain, diabetes, raised prolactin, and sedation.
drugs.overdose_signs: Aripiprazole Oral. Deep sedation, low blood pressure, heart rhythm disturbance, and seizures. This is an emergency.

drugs.medical_uses: Aripiprazole Oral. Psychosis, bipolar disorder, severe agitation, and a few other licensed uses.
drugs.contraindications: Aripiprazole Oral. Other QT-prolonging drugs, other heavy sedatives, and for clozapine a list of blood and cardiac warnings that belong to the prescriber.

drugs.acute_risks: Buprenorphine Hydrochloride. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Buprenorphine Hydrochloride. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Buprenorphine Hydrochloride. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Buprenorphine Hydrochloride. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Buprenorphine Hydrochloride. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Buprenorphine Hydrochloride. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Buprenorphine Hydrochloride. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Buprenorphine Hydrochloride. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Buprenorphine Hydrochloride. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Buprenorphine Hydrochloride. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Remifentanil Hydrochloride. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Remifentanil Hydrochloride. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Remifentanil Hydrochloride. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Remifentanil Hydrochloride. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Remifentanil Hydrochloride. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Remifentanil Hydrochloride. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Remifentanil Hydrochloride. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Remifentanil Hydrochloride. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Remifentanil Hydrochloride. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Remifentanil Hydrochloride. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Citalopram Hydrobromide. Early agitation, and with the wrong mix, serotonin syndrome or a blood-pressure crisis. Overdose of older tricyclics can stop the heart. An antidepressant name on a public medicine listing. Serotonin syndrome and bleeding are the mix risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Citalopram Hydrobromide. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Citalopram Hydrobromide. Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Citalopram Hydrobromide. They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Citalopram Hydrobromide. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.

drugs.medical_uses: Citalopram Hydrobromide. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Citalopram Hydrobromide. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.

drugs.acute_risks: Hydromorphone Hydrochloride. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Hydromorphone Hydrochloride. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Hydromorphone Hydrochloride. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Hydromorphone Hydrochloride. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Hydromorphone Hydrochloride. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Hydromorphone Hydrochloride. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Hydromorphone Hydrochloride. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Hydromorphone Hydrochloride. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Hydromorphone Hydrochloride. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Hydromorphone Hydrochloride. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Zolpidem Tartrate Sublingual. Unconsciousness, choking on vomit, stopped breathing, and accidents. Another sedative, opioid, or benzodiazepine makes this much more dangerous. drugs.chronic_risks: Zolpidem Tartrate Sublingual. Dependence, memory injury, mood change, and for alcohol, liver, heart, and cancer risk.
drugs.overdose_signs: Zolpidem Tartrate Sublingual. Cannot be woken, slow or stopped breathing, blue lips, vomiting while semi-conscious. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Zolpidem Tartrate Sublingual. Physical dependence occurs with repeated heavy use of alcohol, barbiturates, GHB, and related sedatives.
drugs.tolerance: Zolpidem Tartrate Sublingual. Tolerance to the feeling rises faster than tolerance to stopped breathing.
drugs.withdrawal: Zolpidem Tartrate Sublingual. Alcohol, barbiturate, and GHB withdrawal can cause seizures and delirium and can be fatal. Stopping suddenly after heavy use needs medical care.
drugs.medical_uses: Zolpidem Tartrate Sublingual. Some are anaesthetics, antiseizure medicines, or alcohol treatments. Others have no safe nonmedical use.
drugs.contraindications: Zolpidem Tartrate Sublingual. Other sedatives, lung disease, a history of withdrawal seizures, and pregnancy.
drugs.testing: Zolpidem Tartrate Sublingual. Strength of non-pharmaceutical GHB-type liquids is unknowable by looking. Reagents do not make a sedative safe.
drugs.harm_reduction: Zolpidem Tartrate Sublingual. Sedative withdrawal can kill. Do not stop heavy use suddenly without medical help. Do not mix sedatives. This file has no dose.

drugs.chronic_risks: Butalbital, Aspirin, Caffeine and Codeine Phosphate. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Butalbital, Aspirin, Caffeine and Codeine Phosphate. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.

drugs.withdrawal: Butalbital, Aspirin, Caffeine and Codeine Phosphate. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.

drugs.contraindications: Butalbital, Aspirin, Caffeine and Codeine Phosphate. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.

drugs.acute_risks: Acetaminophen and Codeine. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Acetaminophen and Codeine. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Acetaminophen and Codeine. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Acetaminophen and Codeine. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Acetaminophen and Codeine. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Acetaminophen and Codeine. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Acetaminophen and Codeine. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Acetaminophen and Codeine. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Acetaminophen and Codeine. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Acetaminophen and Codeine. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Amphetamine Extended-Release. Heart attack, stroke, seizure, overheating, and agitated psychosis. Risk rises with other stimulants, dehydration, and confined hot spaces. A stimulant name on a public medicine listing. Heart strain, overheating, and a second stimulant are the acute risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Amphetamine Extended-Release. Dependence, exhaustion, weight loss, heart injury, tooth and nasal damage for some, and persistent anxiety or psychosis.
drugs.overdose_signs: Amphetamine Extended-Release. Chest pain, collapsing, extreme agitation, very high temperature, seizures, or a pounding heart. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Amphetamine Extended-Release. Psychological dependence is common. Some stimulants also cause a severe crash.
drugs.tolerance: Amphetamine Extended-Release. The wanted effect fades faster than the strain on the heart.
drugs.withdrawal: Amphetamine Extended-Release. Exhaustion, hunger, low mood, and strong cravings. Suicidal thoughts can appear in the crash.
drugs.medical_uses: Amphetamine Extended-Release. A few are licensed for attention or sleep disorders. Most stimulant material outside a pharmacy is unregulated.
drugs.contraindications: Amphetamine Extended-Release. Heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, psychosis, pregnancy, and MAOI medicines.

drugs.acute_risks: Fentanyl Citrate. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Fentanyl Citrate. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Fentanyl Citrate. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Fentanyl Citrate. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Fentanyl Citrate. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Fentanyl Citrate. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Fentanyl Citrate. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Fentanyl Citrate. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Fentanyl Citrate. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Fentanyl Citrate. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.chronic_risks: Tramadol Hydrochloride and Acetaminophen. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Tramadol Hydrochloride and Acetaminophen. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.

drugs.withdrawal: Tramadol Hydrochloride and Acetaminophen. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.

drugs.acute_risks: Ziprasidone Hydrochloride. Severe stiffness, high fever and confusion can be neuroleptic malignant syndrome, which is an emergency. Some of these drugs prolong the QT interval. drugs.chronic_risks: Ziprasidone Hydrochloride. Movement disorders, weight gain, diabetes, raised prolactin, and sedation.
drugs.overdose_signs: Ziprasidone Hydrochloride. Deep sedation, low blood pressure, heart rhythm disturbance, and seizures. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Ziprasidone Hydrochloride. Not a classic dependence drug. Stopping suddenly can relapse illness and cause withdrawal symptoms.
drugs.tolerance: Ziprasidone Hydrochloride. Sedation may ease. Movement and metabolic harms may not.
drugs.withdrawal: Ziprasidone Hydrochloride. Nausea, sweating, restlessness, and return of the illness being treated. This is a prescriber decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Ziprasidone Hydrochloride. Psychosis, bipolar disorder, severe agitation, and a few other licensed uses.
drugs.contraindications: Ziprasidone Hydrochloride. Other QT-prolonging drugs, other heavy sedatives, and for clozapine a list of blood and cardiac warnings that belong to the prescriber.

effects: reduced agitation
sedation
reduced psychotic intensity over time
adverse_effects: stiffness
restlessness
weight gain
dry mouth
low blood pressure
drugs.acute_risks: Ziprasidone HCl. Severe stiffness, high fever and confusion can be neuroleptic malignant syndrome, which is an emergency. Some of these drugs prolong the QT interval. An antipsychotic name on a public medicine listing. It adds sedation and, for several in the class, a heart-rhythm risk. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Ziprasidone HCl. Movement disorders, weight gain, diabetes, raised prolactin, and sedation.
drugs.overdose_signs: Ziprasidone HCl. Deep sedation, low blood pressure, heart rhythm disturbance, and seizures. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Ziprasidone HCl. Not a classic dependence drug. Stopping suddenly can relapse illness and cause withdrawal symptoms.
drugs.tolerance: Ziprasidone HCl. Sedation may ease. Movement and metabolic harms may not.
drugs.withdrawal: Ziprasidone HCl. Nausea, sweating, restlessness, and return of the illness being treated. This is a prescriber decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Ziprasidone HCl. Psychosis, bipolar disorder, severe agitation, and a few other licensed uses.
drugs.contraindications: Ziprasidone HCl. Other QT-prolonging drugs, other heavy sedatives, and for clozapine a list of blood and cardiac warnings that belong to the prescriber.
drugs.testing: Ziprasidone HCl. Not identified by reagent kits in a useful way.
drugs.harm_reduction: Ziprasidone HCl. Fever plus rigidity on one of these medicines is an emergency. Do not stack with other sedatives for sleep. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Imipramine Pamoate. Early agitation, and with the wrong mix, serotonin syndrome or a blood-pressure crisis. Overdose of older tricyclics can stop the heart. An antidepressant name on a public medicine listing. Serotonin syndrome and bleeding are the mix risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Imipramine Pamoate. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Imipramine Pamoate. Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Imipramine Pamoate. They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Imipramine Pamoate. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Imipramine Pamoate. Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Imipramine Pamoate. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Imipramine Pamoate. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.
drugs.testing: Imipramine Pamoate. Not a reagent-test problem. The risk is the name on the packet plus whatever else is taken.
drugs.harm_reduction: Imipramine Pamoate. Do not combine an MAOI with an SSRI, a stimulant, tramadol, or DXM. Do not stop suddenly without the prescriber. This file has no dose.

drugs.dependence: Lidocaine Cream 4%. Not the usual pattern, except where the drug is also a sedative people return to.

drugs.acute_risks: Fentanyl Transdermal. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Fentanyl Transdermal. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Fentanyl Transdermal. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Fentanyl Transdermal. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Fentanyl Transdermal. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Fentanyl Transdermal. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Fentanyl Transdermal. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Fentanyl Transdermal. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Fentanyl Transdermal. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Fentanyl Transdermal. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

An antidepressant name on a public medicine listing. Serotonin syndrome and bleeding are the mix risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Desvenlafaxine Succinate. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Desvenlafaxine Succinate. Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Desvenlafaxine Succinate. They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Desvenlafaxine Succinate. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Desvenlafaxine Succinate. Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Desvenlafaxine Succinate. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Desvenlafaxine Succinate. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.
drugs.testing: Desvenlafaxine Succinate. Not a reagent-test problem. The risk is the name on the packet plus whatever else is taken.
drugs.harm_reduction: Desvenlafaxine Succinate. Do not combine an MAOI with an SSRI, a stimulant, tramadol, or DXM. Do not stop suddenly without the prescriber. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Codeine Sulfate. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Codeine Sulfate. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Codeine Sulfate. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Codeine Sulfate. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Codeine Sulfate. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Codeine Sulfate. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Codeine Sulfate. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Codeine Sulfate. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Codeine Sulfate. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Codeine Sulfate. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

dry mouth

drugs.acute_risks: Chlorpromazine Hci. Severe stiffness, high fever and confusion can be neuroleptic malignant syndrome, which is an emergency. Some of these drugs prolong the QT interval. An antipsychotic name on a public medicine listing. It adds sedation and, for several in the class, a heart-rhythm risk. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Chlorpromazine Hci. Movement disorders, weight gain, diabetes, raised prolactin, and sedation.
drugs.overdose_signs: Chlorpromazine Hci. Deep sedation, low blood pressure, heart rhythm disturbance, and seizures. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Chlorpromazine Hci. Not a classic dependence drug. Stopping suddenly can relapse illness and cause withdrawal symptoms.
drugs.tolerance: Chlorpromazine Hci. Sedation may ease. Movement and metabolic harms may not.
drugs.withdrawal: Chlorpromazine Hci. Nausea, sweating, restlessness, and return of the illness being treated. This is a prescriber decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Chlorpromazine Hci. Psychosis, bipolar disorder, severe agitation, and a few other licensed uses.
drugs.contraindications: Chlorpromazine Hci. Other QT-prolonging drugs, other heavy sedatives, and for clozapine a list of blood and cardiac warnings that belong to the prescriber.
drugs.testing: Chlorpromazine Hci. Not identified by reagent kits in a useful way.
drugs.harm_reduction: Chlorpromazine Hci. Fever plus rigidity on one of these medicines is an emergency. Do not stack with other sedatives for sleep. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Bupropion Hydrobromide. Early agitation, and with the wrong mix, serotonin syndrome or a blood-pressure crisis. Overdose of older tricyclics can stop the heart. An antidepressant name on a public medicine listing. Serotonin syndrome and bleeding are the mix risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Bupropion Hydrobromide. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Bupropion Hydrobromide. Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Bupropion Hydrobromide. They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Bupropion Hydrobromide. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Bupropion Hydrobromide. Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Bupropion Hydrobromide. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Bupropion Hydrobromide. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.
drugs.testing: Bupropion Hydrobromide. Not a reagent-test problem. The risk is the name on the packet plus whatever else is taken.
drugs.harm_reduction: Bupropion Hydrobromide. Do not combine an MAOI with an SSRI, a stimulant, tramadol, or DXM. Do not stop suddenly without the prescriber. This file has no dose.

adverse_effects: vomiting
amnesia
injury
unconsciousness

drugs.acute_risks: Phenobarbital Sodium. Unconsciousness, choking on vomit, stopped breathing, and accidents. Another sedative, opioid, or benzodiazepine makes this much more dangerous. A sedative name on a public medicine listing. With alcohol, an opioid, or another sedative it can stop breathing. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Phenobarbital Sodium. Dependence, memory injury, mood change, and for alcohol, liver, heart, and cancer risk.
drugs.overdose_signs: Phenobarbital Sodium. Cannot be woken, slow or stopped breathing, blue lips, vomiting while semi-conscious. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Phenobarbital Sodium. Physical dependence occurs with repeated heavy use of alcohol, barbiturates, GHB, and related sedatives.
drugs.tolerance: Phenobarbital Sodium. Tolerance to the feeling rises faster than tolerance to stopped breathing.
drugs.withdrawal: Phenobarbital Sodium. Alcohol, barbiturate, and GHB withdrawal can cause seizures and delirium and can be fatal. Stopping suddenly after heavy use needs medical care.
drugs.medical_uses: Phenobarbital Sodium. Some are anaesthetics, antiseizure medicines, or alcohol treatments. Others have no safe nonmedical use.
drugs.contraindications: Phenobarbital Sodium. Other sedatives, lung disease, a history of withdrawal seizures, and pregnancy.
drugs.testing: Phenobarbital Sodium. Strength of non-pharmaceutical GHB-type liquids is unknowable by looking. Reagents do not make a sedative safe.
drugs.harm_reduction: Phenobarbital Sodium. Sedative withdrawal can kill. Do not stop heavy use suddenly without medical help. Do not mix sedatives. This file has no dose.

sedation

adverse_effects: nausea

confusion

drugs.acute_risks: Buprenorphine HCl. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Buprenorphine HCl. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Buprenorphine HCl. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Buprenorphine HCl. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Buprenorphine HCl. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Buprenorphine HCl. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Buprenorphine HCl. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Buprenorphine HCl. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Buprenorphine HCl. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Buprenorphine HCl. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.chronic_risks: Serdexmethylphenidate and Dexmethylphenidate. Dependence, exhaustion, weight loss, heart injury, tooth and nasal damage for some, and persistent anxiety or psychosis.
drugs.overdose_signs: Serdexmethylphenidate and Dexmethylphenidate. Chest pain, collapsing, extreme agitation, very high temperature, seizures, or a pounding heart. This is an emergency.

drugs.acute_risks: Dextroamphetamine. Heart attack, stroke, seizure, overheating, and agitated psychosis. Risk rises with other stimulants, dehydration, and confined hot spaces. A stimulant name on a public medicine listing. Heart strain, overheating, and a second stimulant are the acute risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Dextroamphetamine. Dependence, exhaustion, weight loss, heart injury, tooth and nasal damage for some, and persistent anxiety or psychosis.
drugs.overdose_signs: Dextroamphetamine. Chest pain, collapsing, extreme agitation, very high temperature, seizures, or a pounding heart. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Dextroamphetamine. Psychological dependence is common. Some stimulants also cause a severe crash.
drugs.tolerance: Dextroamphetamine. The wanted effect fades faster than the strain on the heart.
drugs.withdrawal: Dextroamphetamine. Exhaustion, hunger, low mood, and strong cravings. Suicidal thoughts can appear in the crash.
drugs.medical_uses: Dextroamphetamine. A few are licensed for attention or sleep disorders. Most stimulant material outside a pharmacy is unregulated.
drugs.contraindications: Dextroamphetamine. Heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, psychosis, pregnancy, and MAOI medicines.
drugs.testing: Dextroamphetamine. Reagents can suggest a class and still miss dangerous substitutes such as PMA, synthetic cathinones, or fentanyl in a pressed pill.
drugs.harm_reduction: Dextroamphetamine. Overheating and chest pain are emergencies. Do not mix with other stimulants or MAOIs. This file has no dose and no source.

drugs.acute_risks: Escitalopram Oral. Early agitation, and with the wrong mix, serotonin syndrome or a blood-pressure crisis. Overdose of older tricyclics can stop the heart. An antidepressant name on a public medicine listing. Serotonin syndrome and bleeding are the mix risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Escitalopram Oral. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Escitalopram Oral. Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Escitalopram Oral. They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Escitalopram Oral. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Escitalopram Oral. Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Escitalopram Oral. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Escitalopram Oral. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.
drugs.testing: Escitalopram Oral. Not a reagent-test problem. The risk is the name on the packet plus whatever else is taken.
drugs.harm_reduction: Escitalopram Oral. Do not combine an MAOI with an SSRI, a stimulant, tramadol, or DXM. Do not stop suddenly without the prescriber. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Cocaine Hydrochloride. Heart attack, stroke, seizure, overheating, and agitated psychosis. Risk rises with other stimulants, dehydration, and confined hot spaces. A stimulant name on a public medicine listing. Heart strain, overheating, and a second stimulant are the acute risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Cocaine Hydrochloride. Dependence, exhaustion, weight loss, heart injury, tooth and nasal damage for some, and persistent anxiety or psychosis.
drugs.overdose_signs: Cocaine Hydrochloride. Chest pain, collapsing, extreme agitation, very high temperature, seizures, or a pounding heart. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Cocaine Hydrochloride. Psychological dependence is common. Some stimulants also cause a severe crash.
drugs.tolerance: Cocaine Hydrochloride. The wanted effect fades faster than the strain on the heart.
drugs.withdrawal: Cocaine Hydrochloride. Exhaustion, hunger, low mood, and strong cravings. Suicidal thoughts can appear in the crash.
drugs.medical_uses: Cocaine Hydrochloride. A few are licensed for attention or sleep disorders. Most stimulant material outside a pharmacy is unregulated.
drugs.contraindications: Cocaine Hydrochloride. Heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, psychosis, pregnancy, and MAOI medicines.
drugs.testing: Cocaine Hydrochloride. Reagents can suggest a class and still miss dangerous substitutes such as PMA, synthetic cathinones, or fentanyl in a pressed pill.
drugs.harm_reduction: Cocaine Hydrochloride. Overheating and chest pain are emergencies. Do not mix with other stimulants or MAOIs. This file has no dose and no source.

drugs.chronic_risks: Venlafaxine Hcl. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.

drugs.tolerance: Venlafaxine Hcl. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Venlafaxine Hcl. Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Venlafaxine Hcl. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Venlafaxine Hcl. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.
drugs.testing: Venlafaxine Hcl. Not a reagent-test problem. The risk is the name on the packet plus whatever else is taken.
drugs.harm_reduction: Venlafaxine Hcl. Do not combine an MAOI with an SSRI, a stimulant, tramadol, or DXM. Do not stop suddenly without the prescriber. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Meperidine Hydrochloride. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Meperidine Hydrochloride. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Meperidine Hydrochloride. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Meperidine Hydrochloride. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Meperidine Hydrochloride. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Meperidine Hydrochloride. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Meperidine Hydrochloride. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Meperidine Hydrochloride. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Meperidine Hydrochloride. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Meperidine Hydrochloride. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Ipratropium Bromide Inhalation. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Ipratropium Bromide Inhalation. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Ipratropium Bromide Inhalation. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Ipratropium Bromide Inhalation. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Ipratropium Bromide Inhalation. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Ipratropium Bromide Inhalation. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Ipratropium Bromide Inhalation. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Ipratropium Bromide Inhalation. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Ipratropium Bromide Inhalation. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Ipratropium Bromide Inhalation. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Apomorphine Hydrochloride. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Apomorphine Hydrochloride. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Apomorphine Hydrochloride. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Apomorphine Hydrochloride. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Apomorphine Hydrochloride. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Apomorphine Hydrochloride. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Apomorphine Hydrochloride. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Apomorphine Hydrochloride. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Apomorphine Hydrochloride. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Apomorphine Hydrochloride. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Capsules. Heart attack, stroke, seizure, overheating, and agitated psychosis. Risk rises with other stimulants, dehydration, and confined hot spaces. A stimulant name on a public medicine listing. Heart strain, overheating, and a second stimulant are the acute risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Capsules. Dependence, exhaustion, weight loss, heart injury, tooth and nasal damage for some, and persistent anxiety or psychosis.
drugs.overdose_signs: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Capsules. Chest pain, collapsing, extreme agitation, very high temperature, seizures, or a pounding heart. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Capsules. Psychological dependence is common. Some stimulants also cause a severe crash.
drugs.tolerance: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Capsules. The wanted effect fades faster than the strain on the heart.
drugs.withdrawal: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Capsules. Exhaustion, hunger, low mood, and strong cravings. Suicidal thoughts can appear in the crash.
drugs.medical_uses: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Capsules. A few are licensed for attention or sleep disorders. Most stimulant material outside a pharmacy is unregulated.
drugs.contraindications: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Capsules. Heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, psychosis, pregnancy, and MAOI medicines.
drugs.testing: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Capsules. Reagents can suggest a class and still miss dangerous substitutes such as PMA, synthetic cathinones, or fentanyl in a pressed pill.
drugs.harm_reduction: Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate Capsules. Overheating and chest pain are emergencies. Do not mix with other stimulants or MAOIs. This file has no dose and no source.

drugs.dependence: Anorectal Lidocaine. Not the usual pattern, except where the drug is also a sedative people return to.

drugs.withdrawal: Anorectal Lidocaine. Not the main harm.

changed appetite

drugs.acute_risks: Trimipramine Maleate. Early agitation, and with the wrong mix, serotonin syndrome or a blood-pressure crisis. Overdose of older tricyclics can stop the heart. An antidepressant name on a public medicine listing. Serotonin syndrome and bleeding are the mix risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Trimipramine Maleate. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Trimipramine Maleate. Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Trimipramine Maleate. They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Trimipramine Maleate. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Trimipramine Maleate. Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Trimipramine Maleate. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Trimipramine Maleate. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.
drugs.testing: Trimipramine Maleate. Not a reagent-test problem. The risk is the name on the packet plus whatever else is taken.
drugs.harm_reduction: Trimipramine Maleate. Do not combine an MAOI with an SSRI, a stimulant, tramadol, or DXM. Do not stop suddenly without the prescriber. This file has no dose.

drugs.chronic_risks: Oxycodone Hydchloride. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Oxycodone Hydchloride. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.

drugs.contraindications: Oxycodone Hydchloride. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.

drugs.harm_reduction: Oxycodone Hydchloride. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Bupropion Hydrochloride (xl). Early agitation, and with the wrong mix, serotonin syndrome or a blood-pressure crisis. Overdose of older tricyclics can stop the heart. drugs.chronic_risks: Bupropion Hydrochloride (xl). Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Bupropion Hydrochloride (xl). Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Bupropion Hydrochloride (xl). They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Bupropion Hydrochloride (xl). Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Bupropion Hydrochloride (xl). Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Bupropion Hydrochloride (xl). Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.

drugs.acute_risks: Promethazine, Phenylephrine, Codeine. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Promethazine, Phenylephrine, Codeine. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Promethazine, Phenylephrine, Codeine. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Promethazine, Phenylephrine, Codeine. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Promethazine, Phenylephrine, Codeine. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Promethazine, Phenylephrine, Codeine. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Promethazine, Phenylephrine, Codeine. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Promethazine, Phenylephrine, Codeine. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Promethazine, Phenylephrine, Codeine. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Promethazine, Phenylephrine, Codeine. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.chronic_risks: Levmetamfetamine Nasal Decongestant. Dependence, exhaustion, weight loss, heart injury, tooth and nasal damage for some, and persistent anxiety or psychosis.
drugs.overdose_signs: Levmetamfetamine Nasal Decongestant. Chest pain, collapsing, extreme agitation, very high temperature, seizures, or a pounding heart. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Levmetamfetamine Nasal Decongestant. Psychological dependence is common. Some stimulants also cause a severe crash.
drugs.tolerance: Levmetamfetamine Nasal Decongestant. The wanted effect fades faster than the strain on the heart.
drugs.withdrawal: Levmetamfetamine Nasal Decongestant. Exhaustion, hunger, low mood, and strong cravings. Suicidal thoughts can appear in the crash.
drugs.medical_uses: Levmetamfetamine Nasal Decongestant. A few are licensed for attention or sleep disorders. Most stimulant material outside a pharmacy is unregulated.
drugs.contraindications: Levmetamfetamine Nasal Decongestant. Heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, psychosis, pregnancy, and MAOI medicines.
drugs.testing: Levmetamfetamine Nasal Decongestant. Reagents can suggest a class and still miss dangerous substitutes such as PMA, synthetic cathinones, or fentanyl in a pressed pill.
drugs.harm_reduction: Levmetamfetamine Nasal Decongestant. Overheating and chest pain are emergencies. Do not mix with other stimulants or MAOIs. This file has no dose and no source.
