drugs.acute_risks: Benzhydrocodone and Acetaminophen. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Benzhydrocodone and Acetaminophen. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Benzhydrocodone and Acetaminophen. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Benzhydrocodone and Acetaminophen. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Benzhydrocodone and Acetaminophen. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Benzhydrocodone and Acetaminophen. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Benzhydrocodone and Acetaminophen. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Benzhydrocodone and Acetaminophen. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Benzhydrocodone and Acetaminophen. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Benzhydrocodone and Acetaminophen. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.mechanism: Lidocaine Hci 4%. Either deep central sedation or sodium-channel blockade in nerves and heart.
drugs.onset: Lidocaine Hci 4%. Very fast for induction anaesthetics. Local anaesthetics depend on where they are placed, which this file does not describe.
drugs.duration: Lidocaine Hci 4%. Minutes to hours. Residual impairment after sedation lasts longer than the procedure.

effects: unconsciousness or numbness in medical use
adverse_effects: stopped breathing
low blood pressure
heart rhythm disturbance
nausea
drugs.acute_risks: Lidocaine Hci 4%. Loss of the airway, stopped breathing, and for local anaesthetics, seizures and cardiac arrest if they reach the blood in quantity. An anaesthetic name on a public medicine listing. Outside monitored care it can stop breathing. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Lidocaine Hci 4%. Repeated nonmedical use of volatile anaesthetics injures organs and can sensitise the heart.
drugs.overdose_signs: Lidocaine Hci 4%. Unresponsiveness and no reliable breathing. This is an emergency. Do not wait.
drugs.dependence: Lidocaine Hci 4%. Not the usual pattern, except where the drug is also a sedative people return to.
drugs.tolerance: Lidocaine Hci 4%. Not a useful idea outside anaesthesia. The step from sedated to not breathing is small.
drugs.withdrawal: Lidocaine Hci 4%. Not the main harm.
drugs.medical_uses: Lidocaine Hci 4%. Surgery, procedures, and local pain control, with monitoring.
drugs.contraindications: Lidocaine Hci 4%. No airway support, other sedatives, and certain heart conditions for local anaesthetics.
drugs.testing: Lidocaine Hci 4%. There is no home test that makes an anaesthetic safe to use.
drugs.harm_reduction: Lidocaine Hci 4%. These drugs belong where someone can breathe for the person. This file has no dose and no method.

drugs.acute_risks: Methylphenidate Extended-release. Heart attack, stroke, seizure, overheating, and agitated psychosis. Risk rises with other stimulants, dehydration, and confined hot spaces. A stimulant name on a public medicine listing. Heart strain, overheating, and a second stimulant are the acute risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Methylphenidate Extended-release. Dependence, exhaustion, weight loss, heart injury, tooth and nasal damage for some, and persistent anxiety or psychosis.
drugs.overdose_signs: Methylphenidate Extended-release. Chest pain, collapsing, extreme agitation, very high temperature, seizures, or a pounding heart. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Methylphenidate Extended-release. Psychological dependence is common. Some stimulants also cause a severe crash.
drugs.tolerance: Methylphenidate Extended-release. The wanted effect fades faster than the strain on the heart.
drugs.withdrawal: Methylphenidate Extended-release. Exhaustion, hunger, low mood, and strong cravings. Suicidal thoughts can appear in the crash.
drugs.medical_uses: Methylphenidate Extended-release. A few are licensed for attention or sleep disorders. Most stimulant material outside a pharmacy is unregulated.
drugs.contraindications: Methylphenidate Extended-release. Heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, psychosis, pregnancy, and MAOI medicines.
drugs.testing: Methylphenidate Extended-release. Reagents can suggest a class and still miss dangerous substitutes such as PMA, synthetic cathinones, or fentanyl in a pressed pill.
drugs.harm_reduction: Methylphenidate Extended-release. Overheating and chest pain are emergencies. Do not mix with other stimulants or MAOIs. This file has no dose and no source.

drugs.acute_risks: Morphine Tincture. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Morphine Tincture. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Morphine Tincture. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Morphine Tincture. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Morphine Tincture. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Morphine Tincture. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Morphine Tincture. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Morphine Tincture. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Morphine Tincture. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Morphine Tincture. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

drugs.mechanism: Esketamine Hydrochloride. NMDA receptor antagonism is the common thread. Some also affect dopamine or serotonin.

drugs.duration: Esketamine Hydrochloride. About an hour for some, and many hours for PCP-type drugs.

effects: detachment
analgesia
distorted body sense
anaesthesia at high exposure
adverse_effects: nausea
panic
immobility
agitation
amnesia
drugs.acute_risks: Esketamine Hydrochloride. Immobility, accidents, vomiting while semi-conscious, and a state of being unable to move or speak. With alcohol or opioids, breathing may fail. A dissociative name on a public medicine listing. Airway protection fails when the person cannot sit up. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Esketamine Hydrochloride. Ketamine is linked with severe bladder damage, kidney problems, and memory injury. PCP-type drugs are linked with agitation and prolonged psychosis.
drugs.overdose_signs: Esketamine Hydrochloride. Unresponsiveness, vomiting, slow breathing, seizures, or extreme overheating and agitation with PCP-type drugs. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Esketamine Hydrochloride. Psychological dependence on ketamine is well described. Physical withdrawal is milder than with alcohol or opioids and still unpleasant.
drugs.tolerance: Esketamine Hydrochloride. Tolerance rises quickly with frequent ketamine use.
drugs.withdrawal: Esketamine Hydrochloride. Low mood, anxiety, and cravings. Bladder symptoms do not stop just because use stops, and they need medical care.
drugs.medical_uses: Esketamine Hydrochloride. Ketamine and esketamine have medical roles. Most other dissociatives do not.
drugs.contraindications: Esketamine Hydrochloride. Uncontrolled high blood pressure, psychosis, active bladder disease, and other sedatives.
drugs.testing: Esketamine Hydrochloride. Powders sold as ketamine may be a different dissociative of much longer duration. Reagents do not measure strength.
drugs.harm_reduction: Esketamine Hydrochloride. Bladder pain and blood in urine after ketamine need a clinician, not a pause-and-retry. Do not mix with alcohol or opioids. This file has no dose.

drugs.acute_risks: Temazepam Civ. Amnesia, injury, and sexual vulnerability during blackouts. With alcohol or opioids, breathing can stop. A benzodiazepine name on a public medicine listing. drugs.chronic_risks: Temazepam Civ. Dependence, worsened anxiety between uses, falls in older people, and a hard withdrawal.
drugs.overdose_signs: Temazepam Civ. Extreme sedation. If an opioid or alcohol is also involved: slow breathing and unresponsiveness. That is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Temazepam Civ. Dependence can develop within weeks of regular use.

drugs.chronic_risks: Butalbital, Aspirin, Cafeine, and Codeine Phosphate. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Butalbital, Aspirin, Cafeine, and Codeine Phosphate. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Butalbital, Aspirin, Cafeine, and Codeine Phosphate. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Butalbital, Aspirin, Cafeine, and Codeine Phosphate. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Butalbital, Aspirin, Cafeine, and Codeine Phosphate. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Butalbital, Aspirin, Cafeine, and Codeine Phosphate. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Butalbital, Aspirin, Cafeine, and Codeine Phosphate. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.

drugs.acute_risks: Trazodone Hydrochloride Oral. Early agitation, and with the wrong mix, serotonin syndrome or a blood-pressure crisis. Overdose of older tricyclics can stop the heart. An antidepressant name on a public medicine listing. Serotonin syndrome and bleeding are the mix risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Trazodone Hydrochloride Oral. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Trazodone Hydrochloride Oral. Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Trazodone Hydrochloride Oral. They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Trazodone Hydrochloride Oral. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Trazodone Hydrochloride Oral. Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Trazodone Hydrochloride Oral. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Trazodone Hydrochloride Oral. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.

drugs.acute_risks: Flurazepam Hydrochloride. Amnesia, injury, and sexual vulnerability during blackouts. With alcohol or opioids, breathing can stop. A benzodiazepine name on a public medicine listing. It deepens sedation and, with an opioid or alcohol, can stop breathing. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Flurazepam Hydrochloride. Dependence, worsened anxiety between uses, falls in older people, and a hard withdrawal.

drugs.dependence: Flurazepam Hydrochloride. Dependence can develop within weeks of regular use.

drugs.acute_risks: Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. Heart attack, stroke, seizure, overheating, and agitated psychosis. Risk rises with other stimulants, dehydration, and confined hot spaces. A stimulant name on a public medicine listing. Heart strain, overheating, and a second stimulant are the acute risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. Dependence, exhaustion, weight loss, heart injury, tooth and nasal damage for some, and persistent anxiety or psychosis.
drugs.overdose_signs: Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. Chest pain, collapsing, extreme agitation, very high temperature, seizures, or a pounding heart. This is an emergency.
drugs.dependence: Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. Psychological dependence is common. Some stimulants also cause a severe crash.
drugs.tolerance: Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. The wanted effect fades faster than the strain on the heart.
drugs.withdrawal: Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. Exhaustion, hunger, low mood, and strong cravings. Suicidal thoughts can appear in the crash.
drugs.medical_uses: Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. A few are licensed for attention or sleep disorders. Most stimulant material outside a pharmacy is unregulated.
drugs.contraindications: Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. Heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, psychosis, pregnancy, and MAOI medicines.
drugs.testing: Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. Reagents can suggest a class and still miss dangerous substitutes such as PMA, synthetic cathinones, or fentanyl in a pressed pill.
drugs.harm_reduction: Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. Overheating and chest pain are emergencies. Do not mix with other stimulants or MAOIs. This file has no dose and no source.

drugs.acute_risks: Codeine Phosphate and Chlorpheniramine Maleate. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives multiply that risk. Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Codeine Phosphate and Chlorpheniramine Maleate. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Codeine Phosphate and Chlorpheniramine Maleate. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Codeine Phosphate and Chlorpheniramine Maleate. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Codeine Phosphate and Chlorpheniramine Maleate. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Codeine Phosphate and Chlorpheniramine Maleate. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Codeine Phosphate and Chlorpheniramine Maleate. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Codeine Phosphate and Chlorpheniramine Maleate. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Codeine Phosphate and Chlorpheniramine Maleate. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Codeine Phosphate and Chlorpheniramine Maleate. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.

effects: unconsciousness or numbness in medical use
adverse_effects: stopped breathing
low blood pressure
heart rhythm disturbance
nausea
drugs.acute_risks: Witch Hazel Penylephrine Lidocaine. Loss of the airway, stopped breathing, and for local anaesthetics, seizures and cardiac arrest if they reach the blood in quantity. An anaesthetic name on a public medicine listing. Outside monitored care it can stop breathing. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Witch Hazel Penylephrine Lidocaine. Repeated nonmedical use of volatile anaesthetics injures organs and can sensitise the heart.
drugs.overdose_signs: Witch Hazel Penylephrine Lidocaine. Unresponsiveness and no reliable breathing. This is an emergency. Do not wait.
drugs.dependence: Witch Hazel Penylephrine Lidocaine. Not the usual pattern, except where the drug is also a sedative people return to.
drugs.tolerance: Witch Hazel Penylephrine Lidocaine. Not a useful idea outside anaesthesia. The step from sedated to not breathing is small.
drugs.withdrawal: Witch Hazel Penylephrine Lidocaine. Not the main harm.
drugs.medical_uses: Witch Hazel Penylephrine Lidocaine. Surgery, procedures, and local pain control, with monitoring.
drugs.contraindications: Witch Hazel Penylephrine Lidocaine. No airway support, other sedatives, and certain heart conditions for local anaesthetics.
drugs.testing: Witch Hazel Penylephrine Lidocaine. There is no home test that makes an anaesthetic safe to use.
drugs.harm_reduction: Witch Hazel Penylephrine Lidocaine. These drugs belong where someone can breathe for the person. This file has no dose and no method.

drugs.dependence: Lidocaine Hcl Delay Spray. Not the usual pattern, except where the drug is also a sedative people return to.
drugs.tolerance: Lidocaine Hcl Delay Spray. Not a useful idea outside anaesthesia. The step from sedated to not breathing is small.
drugs.withdrawal: Lidocaine Hcl Delay Spray. Not the main harm.

drugs.contraindications: Lidocaine Hcl Delay Spray. No airway support, other sedatives, and certain heart conditions for local anaesthetics.
drugs.testing: Lidocaine Hcl Delay Spray. There is no home test that makes an anaesthetic safe to use.

Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. drugs.chronic_risks: Acetaminophen, Caffeine, Dihydrocodeine Bitartrate. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Acetaminophen, Caffeine, Dihydrocodeine Bitartrate. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Acetaminophen, Caffeine, Dihydrocodeine Bitartrate. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Acetaminophen, Caffeine, Dihydrocodeine Bitartrate. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Acetaminophen, Caffeine, Dihydrocodeine Bitartrate. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Acetaminophen, Caffeine, Dihydrocodeine Bitartrate. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Acetaminophen, Caffeine, Dihydrocodeine Bitartrate. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.

drugs.acute_risks: Bupropion HCl Er. Early agitation, and with the wrong mix, serotonin syndrome or a blood-pressure crisis. Overdose of older tricyclics can stop the heart. An antidepressant name on a public medicine listing. Serotonin syndrome and bleeding are the mix risks. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Bupropion HCl Er. Withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly, weight and metabolic change with some, and persistent sexual side effects in some people.
drugs.overdose_signs: Bupropion HCl Er. Serotonin syndrome looks like agitation, rigidity, sweating, and a rising temperature. A tricyclic overdose looks like seizures and heart rhythm collapse. Both are emergencies.
drugs.dependence: Bupropion HCl Er. They are not intoxicants in the opioid sense. Stopping suddenly still causes a withdrawal syndrome.
drugs.tolerance: Bupropion HCl Er. Side effects often ease. The interaction risks do not expire.
drugs.withdrawal: Bupropion HCl Er. Dizziness, electric-shock feelings, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms. Tapering is a medical decision.
drugs.medical_uses: Bupropion HCl Er. Depression, anxiety, pain, and smoking cessation, depending on the drug.
drugs.contraindications: Bupropion HCl Er. MAOIs combined with SSRIs, stimulants, tramadol, DXM, or many plant preparations. Recent heart attack for some.
drugs.testing: Bupropion HCl Er. Not a reagent-test problem. The risk is the name on the packet plus whatever else is taken.
drugs.harm_reduction: Bupropion HCl Er. Do not combine an MAOI with an SSRI, a stimulant, tramadol, or DXM. Do not stop suddenly without the prescriber. This file has no dose.

Non-pharmaceutical material may contain fentanyl, nitazenes, or xylazine. An opioid name on a public medicine listing. The acute danger is slowed or stopped breathing, especially with alcohol or a benzodiazepine. Naloxone can wear off first. This file is not a regimen and has no dose.
drugs.chronic_risks: Tramadol/APAP. Tolerance, dependence, constipation, low sex hormones, and fatal overdose are the main long-term harms.
drugs.overdose_signs: Tramadol/APAP. Slow or stopped breathing, blue or grey lips, gurgling, unresponsiveness, pinpoint pupils. This is an emergency. Naloxone can reverse the opioid and may need repeating.
drugs.dependence: Tramadol/APAP. Physical dependence is common with repeated use.
drugs.tolerance: Tramadol/APAP. Tolerance rises with repeated use, then falls after a break. A familiar amount can become fatal after a pause.
drugs.withdrawal: Tramadol/APAP. Withdrawal feels like a severe flu with cramps, sweating, and distress. It is rarely fatal by itself and it raises the chance of returning to use.
drugs.medical_uses: Tramadol/APAP. Some opioids are pain or addiction medicines. Many have no accepted role outside a hospital, or none at all.
drugs.contraindications: Tramadol/APAP. Other sedatives, sleep apnoea, severe lung disease, and unmeasured-strength material.
drugs.testing: Tramadol/APAP. Fentanyl strips and reagent colours miss analogues and do not measure strength. A negative test is not proof of safety.
drugs.harm_reduction: Tramadol/APAP. Do not use alone. Keep naloxone nearby and make sure another person knows how to use it. A blank mix result is not a green light. This file has no dose.
